title: Every Contact value must be a URI with a scheme

cites.quote: The value MUST follow the URI syntax described in Section 3 of [RFC3986]. This means that "mailto" and "tel" URI schemes must be used when specifying email addresses and telephone numbers, as defined in [RFC6068] and [RFC3966].
cites.note: Transcribed from a live fetch of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9116.txt on 2026-10-29 (file sha256 79d19ce7a4a35496981095a27fd992797a9fc4d6f3649c2a1e14f494607c61f9). Lines 296-299. The ABNF agrees: contact-field = "Contact" fs SP uri (§4).

policy_note: The test is a SHAPE check on the scheme: a letter, then letters, digits, '+', '-' or '.', then ':' and at least one non-space character (RFC 3986 §3.1). That is the half of the URI grammar the quoted sentence spells out, and it is the real failure mode: a bare email address or phone number. A full RFC 3986 parser would add a dependency to a pure function for no case this file can plausibly carry. Every Contact value is checked, not only the first.
applicability: A security.txt body with at least one non-empty Contact value. A body with none is security-txt-contact-missing's case.

cases.name: a bare email address with no mailto: scheme
a bare phone number beside a valid mailto: line
an http: value is a URI -- security-txt-web-uri-not-https fires instead
no Contact field -- security-txt-contact-missing fires instead
